label: prop:markov-branching-three-term
title: Branching coherence of the Markov trace reduces to $[m+2]_q + [m]_q = [2]_q\,[m+1]_q$
html:
Proposition. Branching coherence of the Markov trace reduces to [m+2]_q + [m]_q = [2]_q\,[m+1]_q

Let y_{(n-k,k)} = [n-2k+1]_q/[2]_q^{\,n} be the two-row Markov weights of convention D. Then adding a box to a two-row Young diagram is coherent with the trace,

  y_{(n+1-k,\,k)} \;+\; y_{(n-k,\,k+1)} \;=\; y_{(n-k,\,k)},

and this identity is, after clearing [2]_q^{\,n+1}, exactly the three-term recursion

  \boxed{\;\; [m+2]_q \;+\; [m]_q \;=\; [2]_q\,[m+1]_q. \;\;}

One identity, every level of the tower

The Bratteli diagram of the tower H_2(q) \subset H_3(q) \subset \cdots branches a two-row shape \lambda = (n-k,k) into the two shapes obtained by adding a box to the first or the second row. Coherence of a trace with the inclusion means the parent weight is the sum of the two child weights, which for the closed form above is the recursion displayed. With m = n - 2k + 1 the correspondence is exact: the two children carry [m+2]_q and [m]_q, the parent carries [2]_q\,[m+1]_q, and the common denominator [2]_q^{\,n+1} divides out.

The recursion itself has no content beyond the definition of a q-integer. Writing [m]_q = (q^{m}-q^{-m})/(q-q^{-1}) and abstracting X = q^{m}, Y = q^{-m}, the numerators of [m+2]_q, [m]_q and [m+1]_q are Xq^{2} - Yq^{-2}, X - Y and Xq - Yq^{-1}; the denominator q - q^{-1} is common and cancels, leaving a polynomial identity in the ideal generated by q\,q^{-1} = 1. There is no natural subtraction, no division, and no appeal to SU(2).

One hypothesis is genuinely needed rather than defensive: [2]_q \ne 0. Over an ordered field q\,q^{-1} = 1 and q + q^{-1} = 0 are incompatible, and at the substrate parameter [2]_q \ge 2; over \mathbb{C}, however, q^{2} = -1 makes the statement false. The recursion is therefore an identity of the real tower, and the qualification travels with it.

What it buys

Three facts the framework uses separately are the same fact.

  • The isospin weights are branch sums. Restricting from H_3(q) to H_2(q), the totally symmetric and mixed-symmetry blocks both reach the symmetric block of H_2(q), and the mixed-symmetry and antisymmetric blocks both reach the antisymmetric one. That is \mu_+ = y_{(3)} + y_{(2,1)} and \mu_- = y_{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)}, the n = 3 instance.
  • The next level closes the same way, y_{(3)}[H_3] = y_{(4)} + y_{(3,1)} and y_{(2,1)}[H_3] = y_{(3,1)} + y_{(2,2)}, which are the instances at m = 3 and m = 1.
  • The normalisation \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 is the recursion summed over a level: [2]_q^{\,3} = [4]_q + 2[2]_q at three strands and [2]_q^{\,4} = [5]_q + 3[3]_q + 2[1]_q at four, the multiplicities being the Specht dimensions of the surviving shapes.

Nothing in the list is an independent assumption about the trace. Each is the three-term recursion evaluated at a different m, which is why the tower admits a coherent Markov trace at all.
